findings.title: Working-hours boundary check never evaluates the slot's end time
findings.body: In the new working-hours check added to `checkIfIsAvailable`, both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`). `end` should be derived from `slotEndTime` (i.e. slot start + event length) to verify the whole booking fits before the organizer's/fixed host's working hours end. Because `end` duplicates `start`, the check `end > workingHour.endTime` is equivalent to `start > workingHour.endTime`, so a slot whose start is inside the window but whose end (after adding eventLength) extends past the working-hours end time is not flagged as unavailable. This directly undermines the PR's stated goal of correctly respecting a fixed host's hours for round-robin events, allowing bookings that run past a fixed host's actual availability window.

findings.title: Dead code: dayjs instances compared with strict equality always evaluate false
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly created dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false regardless of their represented time, since they are different object references. This branch, apparently intended to detect a zero-duration date override (e.g. representing a fully blocked day), can never trigger. As written this is unreachable/dead logic, and any scenario relying on detecting start === end for an override silently falls through to the later branches instead of being handled as intended.

findings.title: Date-override day matching depends on implicit server-local timezone
findings.body: The date-override day match (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`) builds `dayjs(date.start)` without `.utc()`, so its displayed date/format depends on the Node process's local timezone. `slotStartTime`, however, is explicitly `.utc()`. If the server (or a developer's machine, or CI) is not running with TZ=UTC, this comparison can disagree with the rest of the file, which consistently uses explicit `.utc()`/`.tz()` conversions elsewhere, causing date overrides to be matched to the wrong day or missed entirely depending on deployment environment.

findings.title: No test covers the primary fix: fixed-host date overrides blocking round-robin slots
findings.body: The PR description states its main purpose is to make date overrides of fixed hosts taken into account for round-robin events so slots aren't offered when a fixed host is unavailable. The only test changes add a second timezone assertion to the existing single-user 'Check for Date overrides' test (no scheduling type / no hosts). There is no new test combining a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host that has a date override and a non-fixed round-robin host that is available, to verify that the slot is excluded. Given the newly added/changed availability logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (working hours and date-override checks per fixed host) contains at least one concrete bug (see other findings), this is exactly the scenario that should have automated coverage but does not.

findings.title: Override timezone offset computed from a field that is typed optional without a fallback
findings.body: `const organizerUtcOffset = dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset();` passes `override.timeZone` directly to `.tz()`. `TimeRange.timeZone` (packages/types/schedule.d.ts) is declared optional (`timeZone?: string`), so nothing in the type system guarantees it is set. If any caller of `getSlots`/`getTimeSlots` supplies `dateOverrides` without a `timeZone` (the field was only newly introduced and is only populated by the one call site touched in this PR), `.tz(undefined)` will silently fall back to some default/local timezone behavior rather than failing, producing incorrect offsets and therefore incorrect override slot times instead of a clear error.

findings.title: Override offset adjustment can cross midnight but only the time-of-day is kept
findings.body: The new override start/end computation shifts `override.start`/`override.end` by `offset` minutes (the difference between invitee and organizer UTC offsets) and then extracts only `.hour() * 60 + .minute()`. When the offset difference between organizer and invitee pushes the adjusted time across a day boundary (common for large timezone differences, e.g. near the International Date Line), the date portion is discarded and only the wrapped time-of-day is kept, which can make the override appear to apply on the wrong day or produce an incorrect time window instead of being excluded/moved to the adjacent day.
